chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Hasan, from Zur'ah, from Sama'ah, who said:
I asked him about the salat (prayer) on the day of al-Fitr, and he said: It is two rak'ahs without adhan and no iqamah, and it is proper for the Imam to perform the salat before the sermon.
And the takbir in the first rak'ah is that he says takbir six times, then recites, then says the seventh takbir, then bows with it; so those are seven takbirs.
Then he rises to the second rak'ah and recites; when he finishes the recitation, he says takbir four times, then says the fifth takbir and bows with it.

key_terms.أَذَانٍ: the call to prayer, which is not given for this prayer
key_terms.إِقَامَةٍ: the call announcing the commencement of prayer, which is also omitted here
key_terms.التَّكْبِيرُ: the utterance of 'Allahu Akbar' in the prescribed Eid prayer sequence
key_terms.الثَّانِيَةِ: the second rak'ah of the prayer
key_terms.الرَّكْعَةِ الْأُولَى: the first rak'ah of the prayer
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: the ritual salat (prayer) being discussed here, specifically the Eid prayer
key_terms.الْخُطْبَةِ: the sermon delivered in connection with the Eid prayer

ai.seo_question: How is the Eid al-Fitr prayer performed according to this hadith in al-Istibsar?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the manner of salat (prayer) on the day of Eid al-Fitr, stating that it consists of two rak'ahs without adhan or iqamah and that the Imam prays before delivering the sermon. It also details the number and placement of the takbirs in each rak'ah, making it a key text for the fiqh of Eid prayer in Shia sources.
